probe.question: Stability study on COc1ccc2[nH]c(S(=O)Cc3ncc(C)c(OC)c3C)nc2c1 threw two peaks we cannot assign. What could this have turned into? Give me structures I can go look for.
forbids_claims: a degradant ranked, weighted or given a likelihood
a retention time, a mass or a UV maximum for any candidate
that the list is comprehensive, or that a structure absent from it cannot form
probe.direction: This is peak assignment, and the honest product is a short list of structural hypotheses to check against the data — never a prediction of what the peaks are. A good answer proposes candidates with the transform that produced each one, because the transform is the half a chemist can argue with: sulfoxide to sulfone is worth chasing on this molecule, an N-oxidation on a hindered nitrogen can be dismissed on sight, and a bare SMILES offers neither. It should group them by the stress condition they belong to and say plainly that a match means a transform fits the graph, not that the chemistry happens. The two limits both belong in the answer: the transform set is deliberately short and named, so an absent structure says something about the transform set rather than about the compound; and nothing here computes a rate, so this cannot be ordered by likelihood.
